sentences.sentence: It was a beautiful day.
The sun was shining, the birds chirping, and everyone else was in good spirits, but we were somber, and quiet, but we were content.
Jeff had always been the life of the party, no pun intended.
He was the type of person who made everything better just by being around.
So it came as quite a shock when, one day, I learned that he had a terminal illness.
We all gathered at his house.
His family was there and so were a few close friends.
Jeff was there too; he was sitting on his couch looking a bit weaker than he usually did, but that was expected considering that he didn't have much time left.
But when Jeff spoke up, it wasn't like any other conversation with him.
It was serious.
It was about something that needed to be taken care of.
He talked to me about his wishes.
He asked me if I could help him with what he wanted done.
I was a bit worried because I had never heard of what he wanted, but I agreed to do whatever he needed, and I promised that I would find out how to do it.
A 'sky burial' is a traditional Tibetan Buddhist practice where the body is given to the animals in order to benefit them and to give the deceased peace.
After doing some research, I found out that it would require a monk to perform it and that it was not something that could be done alone.
So the next day, we set up a meeting with the monk and we all went to the local temple for the sky burial.
The monk explained to us the process and the meaning behind the practice.
We also learned that we needed to make sure that the sky was clear and that the birds were active that day.
Luckily, it turned out to be a perfect day for this.
The monk took my friend to a very high altitude.
We waited at the bottom for the sky burial to start.

sentences.sentence: As always it was time to say goodbye.
To my brothers and my sisters, may we brave these elements and meet again.
To my aunt Nimbus who sheltered us, thanks for everything.
I know we haven't seen mom since the beginning but—
The sky was starting to darken, and that only meant one thing; another downpour.
Raindrop was about to see his mom, but he was also about to lose his family.
They lived in a big cloud and were the clouds' way of spreading water around.
Raindrop's siblings, Cloudlet and Cloudlet II, along with Aunt Nimbus, were always ready to spread the clouds’ gifts.
Raindrop looked at his mom in the distance.
She was up high and looking at him through her sunglasses.
She was waiting for them to make their journey to her, and she wanted them to be prepared.
Mom always told him not to worry about the weather, but sometimes when the skies started darkening, you couldn't help but get a little nervous.
Aunt Nimbus, who had been keeping them safe while mom was away, flew out of the cloud and began explaining to the kids about what they needed to do to prepare themselves.
They needed to bring their rain coat with them so they could stay dry and cozy.
Aunt Nimbus also suggested they should have their boots on because mom was going to take them on an adventure!
She even said they might be able to see some new friends in the sky if they were lucky!
So, now it was time to say goodbyes, but the family didn’t want to.
The family didn’t want to leave each other, and they especially didn’t want to go without Aunt Nimbus.
But, they knew that this was just part of being a cloud.
As long as mom was waiting for them in the other cloud, they were going to be okay.

sentences.sentence: It flew by quicker than I could comprehend.
The only thing I could see was the same bored face that the man had.

The common factor in this man's entire life seemed to be boredom.
It seemed like he was born into a world where nothing exciting ever happened, and every moment seemed as dull as the last.
At first, I thought he just had a bad attitude.
But then I saw his family.
They were all the same!
His children weren't any more excited for Christmas than they were for any other day of the year.
His wife never got excited about anything, and she always seemed tired.
It didn't matter what he did, it was all the same.
I couldn't believe how much of a difference even a little excitement could make.
I tried to find the man and tell him to take a vacation, but there seemed to be no way to communicate with anyone.
I didn't really care what I did in these 20 minutes, because the man's life was depressing me.
But then I saw it, something that wasn't boring at all.
I saw a kid running around in a park, playing with their dog.
They were laughing and having fun, just enjoying being alive.
That's when I realized that the problem the man faced wasn't an external one, it was internal.
He simply didn't have the passion to enjoy things, he just needed to change himself.
I guess my trip through this man's life was worth it after all.

sentences.sentence: Karen yawned.
Long nights in nursing were bad enough, but on a psych ward rotation, it was made worse by the instability of some of the patients.
Of course, the old hands on the ward were helping to shield her from some of that.
Today, they had been able to keep most of the unstable patients sedated and the suicidal ones were in constant observation.
Still, Karen found herself feeling rather useless.
She was trying to help them, but it was difficult to do anything.
The only way to be sure was if they made a full recovery.
But that could take days or even months for some of them, which was frustrating when she wanted to help right away.
Karen's shift ended at four o'clock, and it was almost three already.
She decided to walk back home instead of taking the bus, even though it took much longer.
As she was walking, she suddenly heard a scream.
She looked around and noticed that she heard it coming from the hospital.
She ran as fast as she could back to the hospital and saw that there was a person being dragged into one of the rooms.
There wasn't any blood on him, so he must have been knocked unconscious before they brought him in.
When she got inside, it was just a guy who looked to be in his early 20s.
They were calling him Jason.
He was a very calm man, and he told the nurse who had brought him in that he was fine and that nothing had happened.
Karen was still very confused and asked Jason why he was here.
He explained that someone had tried to kill him because he had stopped them from committing suicide.
It turns out that the reason he had gone into shock and fainted was that someone had stabbed him in the back.
As they were talking, a young man walked in who seemed to have been crying.
He introduced himself as James and said he had been the person who had been considering suicide but was stopped by Jason.
